page: Amazon Web Services x8g.medium is an entry-tier memory-optimized instance operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated single-core, single-threaded arm64 AWS Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, supported by 64 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 36 MB L3 cache. The platform is configured with 16.0 GB of RAM, delivering a 16:1 memory-to-core ratio. The configuration contains no dedicated GPUs and features no local instance storage, relying on attached storage over a 1 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-thread performance alongside the constraints of a single-core design. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1740.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating of 1694.19, both situated in average benchmark tiers. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 14.31 GB/sec, placing in the top 25%. Conversely, aggregate multi-core metrics, such as a PassMark CPU score of 982.15, a Geekbench multi-core score of 1742.0, static web serving throughput of 2.4 GB/sec, and Redis SET throughput of 2.4 million operations per second, reflect the throughput ceiling inherent to a single execution thread.

The hardware configuration provides high cost efficiency for memory-heavy use cases by pairing a large 16 GB memory footprint with a single core. This prevents the need to pay for surplus compute cores when workloads only require addressable memory capacity. A primary operational tradeoff is the lack of bundled local NVMe storage and the modest 1 Gbps network baseline, which limits high-throughput I/O pipelines.

Amazon Web Services x8g.medium is best fitted for low-concurrency, memory-bound workloads. Typical deployments include distributed in-memory caching nodes, Redis key-value stores, and small-scale memory-intensive background processing tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services x8g.medium is a memory-optimized cloud instance powered by a dedicated 2.8 GHz arm64 AWS Neoverse-V2 processor featuring 1 vCPU and 1 physical core. Managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it provides 16.0 GB of memory, yielding a dense 16:1 memory-to-core ratio. The server lacks bundled local storage and GPU accelerators, maintaining a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations indicate competent single-threaded capacity, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 1740.0 and 14.31 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, aggregate processing metrics, including a PassMark CPU score of 982.15 and Redis SET throughput of 2.4 million operations per second, are constrained by the single-core architecture. This server offers cost-effective memory density for low-compute, memory-intensive workloads such as in-memory caching, Redis instances, and small memory-resident database tasks.
